title: Config Change Safety Controller & State Reconciliation for Cost-Oriented Batching/Caching
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a Config Change Safety Controller that automatically applies cost-oriented batching and caching recommendations but enforces runtime guardrails and fully reconciles observed vs desired state. This controller should minimize token cost regressions while guaranteeing latency SLOs and providing automatic, explainable safe rollbacks when a change degrades user-facing metrics. It is intended to run in the control plane used by Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can apply a recommended batching/caching config change via a single API call and report a human-readable justification
Changes are first staged to a probing canary group (config probe) for a configurable observation window before broad rollout
Automated rollback triggers fire when any of the defined latency, error-rate, or quality (regression) thresholds are breached
State reconciliation loop converges desired config and observed node state within 2 minutes for 95% of nodes after change
All applied changes are logged in the versioned config ledger and visible in Console rollouts with root cause links
End-to-end integration tests and synthetic load experiments validate rollback behaviour in CI
implementation_plan: Spike: simulate batching/caching changes against replayed request traces and measure latency/cost tradeoffs (2w)
Design: spec controller API, canary probing semantics, guardrail thresholds and reconciliation contract (1w)
Core: implement controller: apply, probe, promote, reconcile, and rollback state machine (3w)
Integrations: wire controller to Console rollouts, runtime telemetry, and config ledger (1w)
Tests: unit tests, e2e with synthetic traffic, chaos tests for partial failures (1w)
Docs & Ops: runbook, dashboard widgets, and ops alerts (1w)
triggers_and_guardrails: Cost delta anomaly: token-per-request cost increases > 12% relative to baseline over 5m -> Alert
P50/P95 latency regressions: absolute increase > 40ms at P50 or > 120ms at P95 for production routes -> Trigger rollback
Error budget impact: customer route error rate increase > 0.2% (absolute) for 1m -> Rollback
Quality regression probe: eval set score drop > 2% for model-output-dependent changes (structured-output or reranking) -> Pause rollout
Stability guard: if more than 15% of nodes fail to apply config within 3m, abort and reconcile
Manual hold: presence of a manual hold flag from Console/SE blocks automated promotion
reconciliation_strategy: Periodic pull and compare: controller polls node-reported active config and compares to desired config ledger
Optimistic apply with idempotent ops: all config changes are applied using idempotent APIs and carry a unique change-id
Divergence detection: when observed != desired for a node, controller attempts remediation up to 3 times with backoff
Escalation: if remediation fails, mark node as degraded and route traffic away using routing policies until fixed
State snapshotting: persist pre-change and post-change snapshots in the ledger for fast diff and rollback
Reconciliation window: reconciler must converge or surface manual remediation tickets within the configured window (default 10m)
test_plan: Unit tests for state machine transitions (apply -> probing -> promote -> rollback)
Replay tests using production trace subset with simulated latency/cost model
Canary scenarios: 1% traffic, 5% traffic, and progressive promotion with failure injection
Chaos tests: simulate partial control-plane partition and node apply failures
Backcompat tests: ensure older runtime agents gracefully ignore unsupported knobs
Integration tests: Console rollout UI triggers controller and shows correct status and artifacts
rollout_plan: Start: apply to a dedicated probe group (config probe) representing 1% of routing weight
Observation: measure for a 10-minute probing window against baseline metrics
Promote: if no guardrail breaches, promote to 10% for 15m, then 50% for 20m, then global
Automated rollback: immediate rollback on any trigger breach with transparent reasoning logged
Manual override: SRE or PM can force abort or hold at any promotion stage via Console
Post-rollback analysis: automated runbook links and postmortem template created for non-trivial rollbacks
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: per-change view showing cost delta, P50/P95 latency, error rate, and example traces
Alert: critical when rollback triggered with direct link to impacted routes and change-id
Trace sampling: increase trace sampling for probe traffic during rollouts
SLO integration: tie controller events to SLO burn-rate detection and incident creation
Audit logs: immutable log of who/what changed configs, visible in Private deployments and Console
